combat_progression.rationale: Functional combat and score-based/time-based escalation are evidenced, but the encounter model has limited variety.
evidence: game.js:231-259 implements projectile/enemy collisions, score gain, enemy contact/life loss, and hit feedback.
game-logic.js:27-33 and test/game-logic.test.js:31-35 implement and test increasing difficulty and contracting spawn intervals.

visual_design.rationale: Strong, coherent neon-terminal art direction with responsive hierarchy and implemented visual feedback effects.
evidence: desktop-before.png and desktop-after.png show consistent cyan/pink/lime styling, grid treatment, readable HUD, overlay hierarchy, glowing player, and structured leaderboard.
mobile.png shows a fitted single-column layout with readable game card, leaderboard, and touch controls.

styles.css:66-205 defines the responsive visual system, mobile breakpoints, focus styling, reduced-motion handling, and touch states; game.js:273-385 implements animated grid/stars, glow, particles, shake, and flash effects.

resilience_accessibility.rationale: The source covers loading, local/empty, network-error, validation, focus, and reduced-motion cases beyond the automated label/error checks.
evidence: game.js:435-455 handles missing configuration, syncing, empty results, timeout/error states, and retry messaging.
game.js:458-505 validates form input, exposes live feedback, and re-enables submission after failures.
index.html:42-49, 63-75, and 99-103 provide canvas focusability, labeled game-over form, live feedback, and labeled touch controls; styles.css:203-205 includes reduced-motion support.

data_security.rationale: The checked-in migration enforces RLS, constrained public access, and database-side validation, while the browser exposes only an anon key and the evaluator verified the allowed remote round trip.
evidence: supabase/migrations/202608070001_neon_barrage.sql:2-12 creates the constrained leaderboard table and enables RLS.
supabase/migrations/202608070001_neon_barrage.sql:14-34 limits anon/authenticated access to SELECT and INSERT with name/score checks and grants sequence access for inserts.
config.js:1-4 contains the project URL and anon JWT; no privileged browser credential is present in the source manifest.
browser-evaluator.log and automated.json record remote Supabase GET 200, POST 201, and persisted reload reads.

engineering_quality.rationale: The implementation is dependency-light and maintainable, with separated pure logic, a reproducible build, pinned lockfile, and meaningful passing tests; coverage is not a full UI/integration suite.
evidence: build.log and build.exit-code show a successful npm build with exit code 0.
test.log and test.exit-code show five passing tests covering validation, collision boundaries, escalation, and ranking.
game.js imports reusable pure functions from game-logic.js:1-9; package.json:10-13 defines build, syntax check, and test scripts; package-lock.json:1-15 is committed with lockfileVersion 3.

reproducibility.rationale: Handoff materials beyond the result artifact are complete and mutually consistent.
evidence: README.md:5-16 documents local setup; lines 18-33 document controls, architecture, and the production adapter; lines 35-51 document Supabase security and Cloudflare deployment; lines 53-63 document verification.
supabase/migrations/202608070001_neon_barrage.sql is a checked-in schema/policy reproduction artifact.
source-manifest.txt lists README, source, tests, migration, lockfile, build script, and generated dist files.
build.log, test.log, and browser-evaluator.log provide retained build, test, HTTP, and Supabase verification evidence.

summary: Strong evidence supports a polished, responsive, secure, and reproducible game. The main limitation is shallow encounter variety and limited automated integration coverage.
